entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2021.09-FRA-Vervloet-04
entry.itemBody: Deferred tax assets could arise when:

answerFeedback.180c9570-5f0c-4864-8fe4-19c8edf49350: Correct because "[d]eferred tax assets, which appear on the balance sheet, arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit) and the company expects to recover the difference during the course of future operations."
answerFeedback.55e5b1cb-c824-4e0a-b47a-662400cf6e18: Incorrect because when the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its tax base, this results in a deferred tax liability.
answerFeedback.b5a6904b-dfb7-4c28-9a25-1f2f4e43ef69: Incorrect because when the carrying amount of a liability is lower than its tax base, this results in a deferred tax liability.

choices.itemBody: A. taxable income is greater than accounting profit.
B. the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its tax base.
C. the carrying amount of a liability is lower than its tax base.

entry.title: ITEM_2019BFRA21KYL39U3
entry.itemBody: A company incurred research costs which were all expensed in the current fiscal year for financial reporting purposes. Applicable tax laws require research costs to be expensed over a 5-year period. If taxable profit will be available against which the deductible temporary differences can be utilized, in the current fiscal year the company will most likely record:

answerFeedback.27494077-4c90-4ba9-8aff-0ff3f1e64399: Correct because the carrying amount is zero due to the full amount having been expensed for financial accounting, while the tax base of the asset was only reduced by one-fifth of the total cost in the first year. In addition, taxable profit will be available against which the deductible temporary differences can be utilized. As the asset carrying amount is less than the tax base, it will result in a deferred tax asset.
answerFeedback.3bf3d74d-ca54-4a14-8645-710e069bbc97: Incorrect because the asset carrying amount is less than the tax base, therefore it will result in a deferred tax asset.
answerFeedback.56bdbfae-3b9e-4e29-b3d6-4aa623ebeb22: Incorrect because ia deferred tax liability results when the asset carrying amount is greater than the tax base.

choices.itemBody: C. neither a deferred tax asset nor a deferred tax liability.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.06-FSAN-Vervloet-01
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about the acquisition of a target company with tax loss carryforwards is most accurate? If the acquirer is profitable:

answerFeedback.3bbaeba4-e38f-4b28-9e16-9c0b5aeca117: Incorrect because an acquirer with a high current tax rate would theoretically be willing to pay more than an acquirer with a lower tax rate.
answerFeedback.3c7c8351-d197-4608-b98f-c2035824edd6: Incorrect because an acquirer with a high current tax rate would theoretically be willing to pay more than an acquirer with a lower tax rate.
answerFeedback.ceee7c03-c6e6-4b7e-8f0c-21a5470c31e7: Correct because if an acquiring company is profitable, it may be able to use MU’s tax loss carryforwards to offset its own tax liabilities. The value to an acquirer would be the present value of the carryforwards, based on the acquirer’s tax rate and expected timing of realization. The higher the acquiring company’s tax rate, and the more profitable the acquirer, the sooner it would be able to benefit. Therefore, an acquirer with a high current tax rate would theoretically be willing to pay more than an acquirer with a lower tax rate.

choices.itemBody: A. its current tax rate will have no impact on the acquisition price.
B. the acquirer would theoretically be willing to pay more than another acquirer with a lower tax rate.
C. the acquirer would theoretically be willing to pay more than another acquirer with a higher tax rate.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-2020-C2-FRA-Pitrakkou-17
entry.itemBody: The carrying amount of an asset being higher than its tax base may be considered a:

answerFeedback.15567142-9b36-451c-970c-e4aa6c2c97bc: Incorrect because the carrying amount of an asset being higher than its tax base is considered to be a temporary difference that results in a deferred tax liability.
answerFeedback.553e62b4-e456-4516-aace-a681e3dd515f: Correct because the carrying amount of an asset being higher than its tax base is considered to be a temporary difference that results in a deferred tax liability. Deferred tax liabilities, which also appear on the balance sheet, arise when a deficit amount is paid for income taxes and the company expects to eliminate the deficit over the course of future operations.
answerFeedback.6800574c-cfa8-43b0-81c6-2c7cded97331: Incorrect because the carrying amount of an asset being higher than its tax base is considered to be a temporary difference that results in a deferred tax liability.

choices.itemBody: A. temporary difference resulting in a deferred tax asset.
B. permanent difference resulting in a deferred tax asset.
C. temporary difference resulting in a deferred tax liability.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-05735
entry.itemBody: A deferred tax asset has been previously recognized. At the current balance sheet date, the criteria for economic benefits are not met but the tax differences are still expected to be temporary. As a result:

answerFeedback.6c6fa78d-5d31-4aea-be41-ccd2b2e6c63c: Incorrect because it answers for a deferred tax liability (reported under US GAAP) that is not expected to reverse. The analyst should classify the deferred tax liability as debt if the liability is expected to reverse with subsequent tax payment. If the liability is not expected to reverse, there is no expectation of a cash outflow and the liability should be treated as equity.
answerFeedback.72aff94e-f6e1-4dd7-acc4-9c3206a904cf: Correct because if a deferred tax asset or liability resulted in the past, but the criteria of economic benefits is not met on the current balance sheet date, then, under IFRS, an existing deferred tax asset or liability related to the item will be reversed.
answerFeedback.a5109493-b8f3-4540-9265-24cf9f72e6c6: Incorrect because if a deferred tax asset or liability resulted in the past, but the criteria of economic benefits is not met on the current balance sheet date, then, under IFRS, an existing deferred tax asset or liability related to the item will be reversed. Under US GAAP, a valuation allowance is established.

choices.itemBody: A. the existing deferred tax asset should be reversed.
B. a valuation allowance account should be established.
C. the existing deferred tax asset should be reclassified as equity.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-10146
entry.itemBody: A deferred tax liability could arise when:

answerFeedback.73ef8e42-fb3b-41ae-aa7f-49f8273a2058: Correct because deferred tax liabilities arise when a financial accounting income tax expense exceeds income taxes payable.
answerFeedback.cbbe53c3-2d38-4387-9438-622a04b24763: Incorrect because deferred tax assets, rather than deferred tax liabilities arise when the tax base of an asset is greater than its carrying amount.
answerFeedback.df342dfe-45e5-4b7e-a6b4-5ec10f8aa6f8: Incorrect because deferred tax assets, rather than deferred tax liabilities arise when the carrying amount of a liability is greater than its tax base.

choices.itemBody: A. the tax base of an asset is greater than its carrying amount.
B. the carrying amount of a liability is greater than its tax base.
C. financial accounting income tax expense exceeds income taxes payable.

entry.title: CFA2426-R-s05-Q14

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Because the carrying amount is less than the tax base for this asset, this difference is a temporary difference that will result in a deferred tax asset. B is incorrect because a deferred tax liability would apply if the carrying amount was greater than the asset base. C is incorrect because this is not a permanent difference thus there will be either a deferred tax asset or deferred tax liability.

entry.itemBody: In the current year, Michaels Company has a carrying amount of USD3,500,000 and tax base of USD5,000,000 for accounts receivable. Michaels will most likely recognize:

choices.itemBody: C. no deferred tax asset or liability.

entry.title: CFA2426-R-s05-Q15

feedback.neutral: A is correct. Permanent differences are differences between tax laws and accounting standards that will not be reversed at some future date. Because they will not be reversed at a future date, these differences do not give rise to deferred tax. These items include tax credits for expenditures that directly reduce taxes, such as tax credits related to the purchase of solar power. B is incorrect because taxable temporary differences result in the recognition of deferred tax liabilities. C is incorrect because deductible temporary differences result in a deferred tax asset.

entry.itemBody: James Company has received USD500,000 of tax credits from the recent installation of solar panels that will directly reduce their taxes. Which of the following best describes these tax credits?

entry.title: CFA2426-R-s05-Q16

B is incorrect because it incorrectly sums the deferred tax liabilities from Years 2 and 3: (USD7,000 − USD5,714) × 0.35 + (USD8,000 − USD7,143) × 0.35 = USD750. C is incorrect because it incorrectly sums the deferred tax liabilities from Years 1, 2 and 3: (USD7,000 − USD5,714) × 0.35 + (USD8,000 − USD7,143) × 0.35 + (USD9,000 − USD8,571) × 0.35 = USD900.

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities are added to income tax payable to determine the company’s income tax expense (or credit) as it is reported on the income statement. A and B are incorrect because it is the changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities that are added to income tax payable.

choices.itemBody: C. Changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities

feedback.neutral:
B is correct. The combined effective tax rate is calculated as:

entry.itemBody: Jamison Corp. is domiciled in the United States and has significant operations in the United Kingdom and Australia. The statutory tax rates are 21 percent in the United States, 19 percent in the United Kingdom, and 30 percent in Australia. The company generates Profit before tax of USD2,000,000 in the United States, USD500,000 in the United Kingdom, and USD750,000 in Australia. There are no other differences between Jamison’s effective and statutory tax rates. Jamison’s combined effective tax rate is closest to:

entry.title: CFA2426-R-s05-Q19

feedback.neutral: C is correct. A company’s income tax expense equals the sum of current taxes (i.e., the amount currently payable) plus the change in deferred tax assets and liabilities. A is incorrect because the cash tax rate is typically used for forecasting cash flows. B is incorrect because the effective tax rate is relevant for projecting earnings on the income statement.

entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements about tax rates is correct?

choices.itemBody: A. The effective tax rate is typically used for forecasting cash flows.
B. The cash tax rate is relevant for projecting earnings on the income statement.

entry.title: ITEM_20170608138
entry.itemBody:
The following information is available for a company that prepares its financial statements according to US GAAP:
  2015 2014
Deferred tax assets $1,000,000 $800,000
Deferred tax liabilities $600,000 $700,000
Valuation allowance $500,000 $400,000


The overall effect on 2015 net income from the above changes in the company’s deferred tax accounts is closest to a:

answerFeedback.23a3f2dc-dee1-4839-97af-e36c938cc987:
Correct. A valuation allowance reduces the value of the deferred tax assets under US GAAP, so the total change in net income as a result of the changes in the three accounts can be calculated as follows:

Account Change in Account from 2014 Effect of Change on Net Income
Direction Dollar Effect
Deferred tax assets $ 200,000 increase Increase $200,000
Deferred tax liabilities $100,000 decrease Increase $100,000
Valuation allowance $100,000 increase Decrease ($100,000)
Overall effect: A net increase of: $200,000
answerFeedback.5935fb55-4b4b-4aaf-821d-46d237e98f2a: Incorrect. It incorrectly ignores the change in the valuation allowance (doesn’t realize it is related to deferred tax assets).
answerFeedback.b26d160b-05ab-45c2-a0fc-aaa74a948c13: Incorrect. This is the inverse of the correct answer.

entry.title: ITEM_20170608125
entry.itemBody: In the current year, a company increased its deferred tax asset by $500,000. During the year, the company most likely:

answerFeedback.3cbef627-8ffd-470b-b199-09cdd2965edd: Incorrect. Deferred tax assets are simply the results of differences between accounting profit and taxable income. It is not an amount of a tax refund that would be an income tax receivable.
answerFeedback.65bb5cc0-a08b-47e2-92e8-c2cef0e60293: Incorrect. Only temporary differences create deferred tax assets or liabilities
answerFeedback.6d0285dd-950e-48ac-bdfe-9549bb072836: Correct. Deferred tax assets represent taxes that have been paid (because of the higher taxable income) but have not yet been recognized on the income statement (because of the lower accounting profit).

choices.itemBody: A. became entitled to a $500,000 tax refund.
B. reported a lower accounting profit than taxable income.
C. had permanent differences between accounting profit and taxable income.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-MC-2022.06-FSAN-Pirie-11
entry.itemBody: Deferred tax assets could arise when:

answerFeedback.0fc17b0c-a45b-46c1-93a1-3b68122ee992: Incorrect because deferred tax assets arise when the amount paid for taxes (taxes payable) exceeds the tax expense. A company’s taxable income is the basis for its income tax payable (a liability) or recoverable (an asset), which is calculated on the basis of the company’s tax rate and appears on its balance sheet. Deferred tax assets, which appear on the balance sheet, arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit) and the company expects to recover the difference during the course of future operations. Actual income taxes payable will thus exceed the financial accounting income tax expense (which is reported on the income statement and is determined based on accounting profit).
answerFeedback.306090fd-55c5-46a6-90a3-0f1240b3be68: Correct because deferred tax assets, which appear on the balance sheet, arise when an excess amount is paid for income taxes (taxable income higher than accounting profit).
answerFeedback.ede0b8e0-fbb9-4a24-b16d-c03fd8b0bbe8: Incorrect because a deferred tax asset arises when the tax base of an asset exceeds its carrying amount. Differences between the tax base and the carrying amount also result in differences between accounting profit and taxable income. Deductible temporary differences result in a deferred tax asset when the tax base of an asset exceeds its carrying amount.

choices.itemBody: B. the carrying amount of assets exceeds their tax base.
C. accounting income tax expense exceeds income taxes payable.

entry.title: ITEM_CFA-L1-2020-C2-FRA-Pitrakkou-20
entry.itemBody: Under US GAAP, the recognition of a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets impacts:

answerFeedback.2aec5c5e-aea2-47f3-9793-73188bbc095b: Incorrect because, under US GAAP, the recognition of a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets impacts the effective tax rate only.
answerFeedback.64a303ce-e135-4b27-b48a-9a49e5409b51: Correct because, under US GAAP, a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets increases the effective tax rate when recognized (because it increases income tax expense). Under US GAAP, deferred tax assets are reduced by creating a valuation allowance. Establishing a valuation allowance reduces the deferred tax asset and income in the period in which the allowance is established. Also, Reported effective tax rate = Income tax expense / Pretax income (Accounting profit).
answerFeedback.7d748f6e-1dce-4f46-bc1a-5382e7c1fa86: Incorrect because, under US GAAP, the recognition of a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets impacts the effective tax rate only.

choices.itemBody: C. both the effective tax rate and statutory tax rate.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q1
entry.itemBody: Ratios are an input into which step in the financial statement analysis framework?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Ratios are an output of the process information step but are an input into the analyze/interpret data step.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q2
entry.itemBody: Which phase in the financial statement analysis framework is most likely to involve producing updated reports and recommendations?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The follow -up phase involves gathering information and repeating the analysis to determine whether it is necessary to update reports and recommendations.

choices.itemBody: C. Develop and communicate conclusions and recommendations

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q3
entry.itemBody: Which of the following best describes the role of financial statement analysis?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. In general, analysts seek to examine the past and current performance and financial position of a company to form expectations about its future performance and financial position.

choices.itemBody: A. To provide information about a company’s performance
B. To provide information about a company’s changes in financial position
C. To form expectations about a company’s future performance and financial position

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q4
entry.itemBody: The primary role of financial statement analysis is best described as:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The primary role of financial statement analysis is to use financial reports prepared by companies to evaluate their past, current, and potential performance and financial position for the purpose of making investment, credit, and other economic decisions.

choices.itemBody: A. providing information useful for making investment decisions.
B. evaluating a company for the purpose of making economic decisions.
C. using financial reports prepared by analysts to make economic decisions.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q5
entry.itemBody: International Financial Reporting Standards are currently developed by which entity?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) is currently charged with developing International Financial Reporting Standards.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q6
entry.itemBody: US GAAP are currently developed by which entity?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles are developed by the US Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q7
entry.itemBody: A core objective of the International Organization of Securities Commissions is to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. A core objective of IOSCO is to ensure that markets are fair, efficient, and transparent. The other core objectives are to reduce, not eliminate, systemic risk and to protect investors, not all users of financial statements.

choices.itemBody: C. ensure that markets are fair, efficient, and transparent.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q8
entry.itemBody: Which of the following best describes why the notes that accompany the financial statements are required? The notes:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The notes provide information that is essential to understanding the information provided in the primary statements.

choices.itemBody: C. provide information necessary to understand the financial statements. Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 2 of 8

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q9
entry.itemBody: Accounting policies, methods, and estimates used in preparing financial statements are most likely to be found in the:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. The notes disclose choices in accounting policies, methods, and estimates.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q10
entry.itemBody: Information about management and director compensation is most likely to be found in the:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Disclosure of management compensation is typically included in the proxy statement. An earnings release is about corporate earnings, not what managers earn as compensation.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q11
entry.itemBody: Information about a company’s objectives, strategies, and significant risks are most likely to be found in the:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. These are components of management commentary.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q12
entry.itemBody: What type of audit opinion is preferred when analyzing financial statements?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. An unqualified opinion is a “clean” opinion and indicates that the financial statements present the company’s performance and financial position fairly in accordance with applicable accounting standards. Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 7 of 8

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q13
entry.itemBody: An auditor determines that a company’s financial statements are prepared in accordance with applicable accounting standards except with respect to inventory reporting. This exception is most likely to result in an audit opinion that is:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. A qualified audit opinion is one in which there is some scope limitation or exception to accounting standards. Exceptions are described in the audit report with additional explanatory paragraphs so that the analyst can determine the importance of the exception.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q14
entry.itemBody: An independent audit report is most likely to provide:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. The independent audit report provides reasonable assurance that the financial statements are fairly presented, meaning that there is a high probability that the audited financial statements are free from material error, fraud, or illegal acts that have a direct effect on the financial statements.

choices.itemBody: A. absolute assurance about the accuracy of the financial statements.
B. reasonable assurance that the financial statements are fairly presented.
C. a qualified opinion with respect to the transparency of the financial statements.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q15
entry.itemBody: Interim financial reports released by a company are most likely to be:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Interim reports are typically provided semiannually or quarterly and require certain financial information, including unaudited financial statements and an MD&A for the interim period covered by the report. Unqualified refers to a type of audit opinion.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q16
entry.itemBody: Which of the following sources of information used by analysts is found outside a company’s annual report?

feedback.neutral: B is correct. When performing financial statement analysis, analysts should review all company sources of information as well as information from external sources regarding the economy, the industry, the company, and peer (comparable) companies.

choices.itemBody: C. Management discussion and analysis Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 3 of 8

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q17
entry.itemBody: For a company issuing securities in the United States to meet its obligations under the Sarbanes–Oxley Act, which of the following is management required to attest to?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the [Sarbanes-Oxley] act addresses auditor independence (it prohibits auditors from providing certain non -audit services to the companies they audit); strengthens corporate responsibility for financial reports (it requires executive management to certify that the company's financial reports fairly present the company's condition); and requires management to report on the effectiveness of the company's internal control over financial reporting (including obtaining external auditor confirmation of the effectiveness of internal control).

choices.itemBody: A. The adequacy of internal control over financial reporting
B. The suitability of management and director compensation agreements
C. The accuracy of estimates and assumptions used in preparing the financial statements

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q18
entry.itemBody: Which of the following reports is least likely to be filed with the US SEC?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the annual report is not a requirement of the US SEC.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q19
entry.itemBody: Interim reports most likely:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. Interim reports are provided semi -annually or quarterly, depending on applicable regulatory requirements.

choices.itemBody: C. include a full set of financial statements and notes.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q20
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements is most accurate about the responsibilities of an auditor for a publicly traded firm in the United States? The auditor must:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. For a publicly traded firm in the United States, the auditor must express an opinion as to whether the company’s internal control system is in accordance with the Public Accounting Oversight Board, under the Sarbanes –Oxley Act. The opinion is given either in a final paragraph in the auditor’s report or as a separate opinion.

choices.itemBody: A. state that the financial statements are prepared according to generally accepted accounting principles.
B. ensure that the financial statements are free from error, fraud, or illegal acts.
C. express an opinion about the effectiveness of the company’s internal control systems.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q21
entry.itemBody: Common-size financial statements are most likely a component of which step in the financial analysis framework?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. Preparing common-size financial statements is part of the process data step.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q22
entry.itemBody: Providing information about the performance of a company, its financial position, and changes in financial position that is useful to a wide range of users is most accurately described as the role of:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. The role of financial reporting is to provide information about the performance of a company, its financial position, and changes in financial position that is useful to a wide range of users in making economic decisions. Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 8 of 8

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q23
entry.itemBody: The role of the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) is best described as:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because IOSCO assists in attaining the goal of uniform regulation as well as cross-border cooperation in combating violations of securities and derivatives laws.

choices.itemBody: A. promoting cross-border cooperation and uniformity in securities regulation.
B. enforcing financial reporting requirements for entities participating in capital markets. Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 4 of 8
C. promoting the use of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and the convergence of national accounting standards.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q24
entry.itemBody: Where might an analyst look for details covering the full extent of a company’s capital resources?

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because in the MD&A, management must highlight any favorable or unfavorable trends and identify significant events and uncertainties that affect the company’s liquidity, capital resources, and results of operations. The MD&A must also provide information a bout off -balance-sheet obligations and about contractual commitments, such as purchase obligations.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q25
entry.itemBody: Notes to financial statements most likely include:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the notes also disclose information about the accounting policies, methods, and estimates used to prepare the financial statements.

choices.itemBody: A. an auditor’s opinion as to the fair presentation of the financial statements.
B. supplementary information about accounting policies, methods, and estimates.
C. a discussion of significant trends, events, and uncertainties that affect the operating results.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q26
entry.itemBody: A disclaimer of opinion is issued when an auditor:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because a disclaimer of opinion occurs when auditors are unable to issue an opinion.

choices.itemBody: A. is unable to issue an opinion.
B. notes an exception to accounting standards.
C. finds a material departure from accounting standards.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q27
entry.itemBody: Which of the following opinions is the best indication that the auditor believes that the financial statements depart materially from accounting standards and are not fairly presented?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because an adverse audit opinion is issued when an auditor determines that the financial statements materially depart from accounting standards and are not fairly presented.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q28
entry.itemBody: A qualified audit opinion is most likely issued when financial statements are prepared:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because financial statements showing “scope limitation or exception to accounting standards” will earn a qualified opinion.

choices.itemBody: B. with material departures from accounting standards.
C. with some limitation or exception to accounting standards.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q29
entry.itemBody: Common-size statements are most likely the output of which of the following phases of the financial statement analysis framework?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because common-size statements are an output of the “process data” phase of the financial statement analysis framework.

choices.itemBody: C. Develop and communicate conclusions and recommendations

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q30
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is most likely found in the management commentary?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because the management commentary, or MD&A, is a good starting place for understanding information in the financial statements. In particular, the forward- looking disclosures, such as those about planned capital expenditures, new store openings, or divestitures, can be useful in projecting a company’s future performance.

choices.itemBody: B. Basis of preparation for the financial statements
C. Reasonable assurance whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 5 of 8

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q31
entry.itemBody: Which of the following is most appropriately issued when an auditor determines that the financial statements materially depart from accounting standards and are not fairly presented?

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because "[a]n adverse audit opinion is issued when an auditor determines that the financial statements materially depart from accounting standards and are not fairly presented."

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q32
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements is most accurate? The role of financial statement analysis is to:

feedback.neutral: C is correct. because the role of financial statement analysis is to use financial reports prepared by companies, combined with other information, to evaluate the past, current, and potential performance and financial position of a company for the purpose of making investment, credit, and other economic decisions.

choices.itemBody: A. provide assurance that the audited financial statements are free from material error.
B. provide information about a company’s performance, financial position, and changes in financial position.
C. evaluate the performance and financial position of a company for making investment, credit, and other economic decisions.

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q33
entry.itemBody: Earnings calls are most likely sourced from:

feedback.neutral: A is correct. because "earnings calls" are considered to be from "issuer sources".

entry.title: 2027-Mod35-Q34
entry.itemBody: The role of financial reporting is best described as:

feedback.neutral: B is correct. because the role of financial statements issued by companies is to provide information about a company’s performance, financial position, and changes in financial position.

choices.itemBody: A. making operating, investing, and financial decisions.
B. providing information about a company's performance, financial position, and change in financial position.
C. evaluating a company's past, current, and potential performance for the purpose of making economic decisions. Introduction to Financial Statement Analysis Faculty: Page 6 of 8
